Let \(K=\mathbb C(x)\), and write
\[
a=x(x-1),\qquad b=x(x+1).
\]
The classes of \(a,b\) are independent modulo \(r\)-th powers: if \(a^i b^j\) were an \(r\)-th power with \(0\le i,j<r\), then looking at valuations at \(x=1\) and \(x=-1\) gives \(r\mid i\) and \(r\mid j\). Hence
\[
[\mathbb C(C):\mathbb C(x)]=r^2.
\]

The cover \(C\to \mathbb P^1_x\) is abelian of degree \(r^2\). Its branch data are read from the valuation vectors of \((a,b)\):

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
x & (v_x(a),v_x(b)) & e_x\\ \hline
-1&(0,1)&r\\
0&(1,1)&r\\
1&(1,0)&r\\
\infty&(-2,-2)&r/h
\end{array}
\]
where \(h=\gcd(r,2)\). Therefore Riemann-Hurwitz gives
\[
2g(C)-2
=-2r^2+3r^2\left(1-\frac1r\right)
+r^2\left(1-\frac{h}{r}\right),
\]
so
\[
g(C)=1+r^2-\frac{(3+h)r}{2}.
\]

Now count the fixed points of \(\tau(x,y,z)=(-x,z,y)\). A fixed point must lie over a fixed point of \(x\mapsto -x\), so only over \(x=0\) or \(x=\infty\).

Over \(x=0\), put \(t=z/y\). Then
\[
t^r=\frac{x+1}{x-1},
\]
so above \(0\), \(t^r=-1\), and \(\tau\) sends \(t\mapsto t^{-1}\). Thus a fixed point requires \(t=t^{-1}\), hence \(t=\pm1\). This is compatible with \(t^r=-1\) only for \(t=-1\) and \(r\) odd. So there is one fixed point over \(0\) if \(r\) is odd, and none if \(r\) is even.

Over \(\infty\), again \(t=z/y\), so \(t^r\to1\).

If \(r\) is odd, the points over \(\infty\) are indexed by \(t^r=1\), and \(\tau\) sends \(t\mapsto t^{-1}\). The only fixed value is \(t=1\), giving one fixed point.

If \(r\) is even, write \(m=r/2\) and
\[
A=\frac{y^m}{x},\qquad B=\frac{z^m}{x}.
\]
At \(\infty\), \(A=\alpha=\pm1\), \(t=\lambda\) with \(\lambda^r=1\), and \(B=\alpha\lambda^m\). Since \(x\mapsto -x\),
\[
\tau(A)=-B=-A t^m,\qquad \tau(t)=t^{-1}.
\]
A fixed point requires \(\lambda=\lambda^{-1}\), so \(\lambda=\pm1\), and also
\[
\alpha=-\alpha\lambda^m,
\]
i.e. \(\lambda^m=-1\). This happens exactly when \(\lambda=-1\) and \(m\) is odd, namely \(r\equiv2\pmod4\). Then \(\alpha=\pm1\), giving two fixed points. If \(4\mid r\), there are none.

Thus the number of fixed points of \(\tau\) is
\[
N=2(1-\epsilon).
\]

Finally, Riemann-Hurwitz for the quotient map \(C\to C/\langle\tau\rangle\) gives
\[
2g(C)-2=2\bigl(2g(C/\langle\tau\rangle)-2\bigr)+N.
\]
Hence
\[
g(C/\langle\tau\rangle)
=\frac{2g(C)+2-N}{4}
=\frac{2r^2+2+2\epsilon-(3+h)r}{4}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\displaystyle \frac{2r^2+2+2\epsilon-(3+h)r}{4}}
\]
